title: SLO-driven rollout constraints playbook
summary: Working draft for a rollout UX that lets operators map SLA/SLO constraints to staged rollouts (canary + A/B) and define automatic constraint-driven actions (pause, throttle, rollback, degrade to cheaper model). Goal: make rollouts safety-first by default and provide clear operator affordances when SLOs are close to breach.
wireframes_and_notes:
High-level wireframe ideas (quick sketches):

- Global SLO binding panel (left rail): shows active SLOs for the tenant: latency p95, p99, error rate, availability, quality regression (eval score). Each SLO can be pinned to rollout rules.
- Stage composer canvas (center): horizontal stages: baseline -> canary -> ramp -> full. Each stage displays: traffic %, duration, SLO bindings, automatic actions on breach. Operator can drag-drop SLOs into a stage.
- Stage compact view (collapsed): shows only traffic % + red/yellow/green SLO badges. Hover expands to show recent metrics and recommended action templates.
- Action editor flyout: text fields + quick-presets (pause, throttle 50%, rollback to model X, fallback to variant Y, notify slack channel). Include cooldown period and minimum evaluation window.

Microcopy examples:
- Stage title placeholder: "Canary (5%) — short check window"
- SLO badge tooltip: "p99 latency ≤ 120ms — measured over last 5m (critical)"
- Action confirmation modal: "You’re about to attach an automatic rollback that triggers when p99 > 200ms for 3 consecutive 1m windows. This will re-route traffic to Model v2.1. Continue?"

Accessibility note: color alone cannot be used to convey SLO state; include clear iconography and text labels for each badge.

Performance concerns: retrieving near-real-time SLO metrics for many concurrent rollouts must be offloaded to a dedicated metrics cache to avoid console flakiness. Show cached recency timestamp in hover (e.g., "metrics last refreshed 12s ago").
operator_journey:
Operator scenario: upgrade base LLM from v2.2 -> v3.0 for chat completion.

1) Start a new staged rollout. Choose baseline = v2.2; target = v3.0.
2) Compose stages: Canary (5% traffic, 15m), Ramp (30% traffic, 45m), Full (100%).
3) Bind SLOs: attach p99 latency and eval-quality delta (> -1% regression fails).
4) Select automatic actions: Canary: on p99 breach -> throttle to 2% then notify ops; on quality regression -> immediate rollback. Ramp: on p99 breach -> pause and escalate.
5) Preview shows worst-case scenario timeline and cost delta. Operator hits "Start rollout".

During rollout:
- Console shows per-stage live card: last 1m p95/p99, error rate, eval-quality quick check, and suggested action button ("pause", "rollback").
- If SLO approaches threshold, the stage card pulses amber and the action button is prominent.
- Operator can manually trigger actions; automatic actions run after configured cooldowns.

Post-rollout:
- Rollout report aggregates time-in-stage, SLO briefings, operator interventions, and cost impact. Store report as artifact with links to metrics and relevant tickets.
edge_cases_and_guardrails:
Planned guardrails and edge cases to consider:

- Flapping metrics: require N consecutive evaluation windows to avoid oscillation (configurable by operator).
- Partial telemetry blackout: if metrics pipeline is degraded, fallback to conservative policy (auto-pause rollouts, route to baseline).
- Interleaved rollouts: when two rollouts touch same model variant, provide conflict resolution UI and suggested merge or queuing semantics.
- Low-traffic services: SLOs may be statistically noisy. Provide a min-sample-size threshold before enabling automatic actions.
- Cost spike protection: optional rule to cap added token spend per rollout; if exceeded, throttle traffic and notify finance.
- Cross-region consistency: for multi-region rollouts, allow region-level SLO bindings and region-scoped actions.

Safety defaults (proposal):
- By default, attach "pause on SLO breach" to canaries and require explicit opt-in for automated rollback.
- Require an operator-approved policy for any action that performs automatic model replacement.

open_questions:
Open questions for product/eng review: 

- Which SLO types should be first-class? (suggest: latency p99/p95, error rate 5xx, model-eval-quality delta)
- Should we surface model cost-per-token in the same UI to make tradeoffs explicit?
- How granular should automatic-action scoping be (stage-only vs. global policy)?
- What audit/logging guarantees do legal/compliance need for auto-rollback actions?
- Does dedicated/dedicated-private deployments need a different default safety posture?
